A keyword that hangs — a network call that never returns, an element that never
appears — can freeze an entire run. A **timeout** caps how long a test (or a
single keyword) may take. When the limit is exceeded, Robot Framework stops that
test and fails it, and the run moves on instead of hanging forever.

Set `[Timeout]` on a test, or `Test Timeout` in `*** Settings ***` to cap every
test in the suite.

## Task 1 — Stop a slow keyword with a timeout

**Goal:** create `checks/guarded.robot` with a test whose `[Timeout]` stops a
deliberately slow keyword — proving the guard fires instead of waiting the full
time.

Here is the same idea with a different limit and delay. Adapt it to a `0.3s`
timeout over a `3s` sleep.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Capped At One Second
    [Timeout]    1s
    Sleep    5s
    Log    never reached
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the test `Guarded Against Hangs` is stopped by its timeout.

<!-- hint -->
Put the timeout first in the test, then a keyword that would take much longer:
`[Timeout]    0.3s` then `Sleep    3s`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
The `Sleep` never finishes — the timeout fires at `0.3s` and fails the test with
a "Test timeout ... exceeded" message. That is the guard working.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Guarded Against Hangs
    [Timeout]    0.3s
    Sleep    3s
    Log    never reached
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it and watch the guard fire

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks/guarded.robot
```

The test stops itself the moment the limit is hit:

```terminal
$ uv run robot checks/guarded.robot
==============================================================================
Guarded
==============================================================================
Guarded Against Hangs                                                 | FAIL |
Test timeout 300 milliseconds exceeded.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 test, 0 passed, 1 failed
==============================================================================
```

It fails in about `0.3s` with `Test timeout 300 milliseconds exceeded` — not
after the full `3s`. A real hang would be caught the same way.

**Check:** the run stops the slow keyword at the timeout.
